title: Latin American food stands out in more of NYC than any other cuisine
description: Every spot in New York City, colored by the cuisine that is most over-represented among the restaurants within 500 m compared with its share of all NYC restaurants. Of 1,081 spots where one cuisine stands out, Latin American food (Latin American, Mexican, Spanish, Peruvian and Tex-Mex) leads in 287; colors group the 37 cuisines into eight families. The tightest clusters: Eastern European in Brighton Beach (51× its city share), Korean in Murray Hill, Queens (39×), Kosher in Homecrest (35×) and Caribbean in East Flatbush (24×). Switch to One cuisine to explore any of the 37: Chinatown, Little Italy and Koreatown aren't where their cuisines are most concentrated. Chinese peaks in Sunset Park, Italian on Arthur Avenue in the Bronx, Korean in Murray Hill, Queens. Data: NYC DOHMH Restaurant Inspection Results, restaurants inspected since 2023.
